claim: Mick Wall, Classic Rock 191, 6 Nov 2013: Atlantic meeting in New York January 1979 agreed AC/DC needed a new producer to crack America; George Young stepped aside; Mutt Lange, 31, had produced the Boomtown Rats' No. 1 hit; basic tracking began Saturday March 24 at Roundhouse Studios, recording completed three weeks later on April 14; Atlantic disliked the album title and tried to get it changed; first AC/DC album to crack the US Top 20, eventually selling more than seven million copies; no earlier AC/DC album had gained traction in America

Geoff Barton, 14 May 2018: Atlantic cherry-picked songs from the two Australia-only albums for the international High Voltage; majority from T.N.T., only Little Lover and She's Got Balls from High Voltage; first non-Albert Productions release; UK tour began June 11 1976 at Glasgow City Hall and ended July 7 at London Lyceum, 19 dates; international Dirty Deeds had subtly different versions; Dirty Deeds not released officially in the US until March 1981 because Atlantic execs had misgivings about Scott's gritty vocal style; Scott died February 1980
bio: 'raw, proto-punk alternative to overblown '70s fare'; lists T.N.T. (1975) and Highway to Hell (1979); inducted 2003

formed Sydney November 1973 by Malcolm and Angus Young; name from sister Margaret and sewing machine AC adapter; Scott joined September 1974 after working as chauffeur; logo by Gerard Huerta 1977 first on Let There Be Rock; Vanda and George Young producers; Rock Hall 2003; Scott died seven months after Highway to Hell, Brian Johnson recruited, Back in Black 1980

albums: High Voltage (Australasia) 17 Feb 1975; T.N.T. 1 Dec 1975; High Voltage (international) 14 May 1976 US peak 146; Dirty Deeds 20 Sep 1976; Let There Be Rock 21 Mar 1977 US 154; Powerage 5 May 1978 US 133; If You Want Blood 13 Oct 1978 US 113; Highway to Hell 27 Jul 1979 US 17, RIAA 8x Platinum. Singles: Highway to Hell US Hot 100 47; UK peaks High Voltage 48, Long Way to the Top 55, Dirty Deeds 47, Whole Lotta Rosie 36, Rock 'n' Roll Damnation 24; T.N.T., Jailbreak, Problem Child, Let There Be Rock, Girls Got Rhythm no UK or US chart entry
written by Angus Young, Malcolm Young and Bon Scott, Angus credited for the riff; single released 27 July 1979, same day as album; title from constant touring; produced by Mutt Lange
